transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Sentinel Head of Security), Ethan (Cloud Architect), Lena (Compliance), Tom (Procurement)

-----
Summary (auto): Quick posture review, establish evidence access pattern, validate SAML/SCIM flow, confirm KMS BYOK options and data residency. Action items and follow-ups recorded.

[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, I'm the AE here. Diego, our solutions engineer, is with me. Can we do quick intros?
[00:00:10] Priya (Sentinel): Hi, Priya Kapoor, Head of Security at Sentinel Healthcare. Our main asks today are SOC 2 evidence access and how Redwood would map to our control set.
[00:00:18] Ethan (Sentinel): Ethan Moore, Cloud Architect. I'll be the technical lead on networking and residency details.
[00:00:23] Lena (Sentinel): Lena Ortiz, Compliance. I'll be looking at evidence workflows and retention.
[00:00:28] Tom (Sentinel): Tom Reeves, Procurement — listening for procurement/contract milestones.
[00:00:33] Maya: Great. Diego, do you want to frame what we'll cover?
[00:00:36] Diego (Redwood SE): Yep. We'll run through our SOC 2 Type II scope, ISO 27001 cert, then show the Trust Center access model — read-only evidence buckets, API pulls, and SAML based gating. Then we'll dive into SSO/SCIM and BYOK options. We'll also talk about logs — what we capture, formats, retention.
[00:00:51] Priya: Quick question up front — does Redwood provide the full SOC 2 report or a short trust pack?
[00:00:58] Maya: We can share the full Type II report under an NDA — we typically provide it to security teams. Also a trust pack with the scope and control narratives. We'll kick that over after the call.
[00:01:06] Priya: Great. That helps.
[00:01:09] Diego: For ISO 27001, we have a certificate and a high level scope doc. It's not the full ISMS doc but shows in-scope services and control owners.

[00:01:22] Ethan: For evidence access, we're trying to avoid SFTP or manual uploads. What's the typical integration?
[00:01:28] Diego: Two patterns: 1) Trust Center read-only access — we create a read-only tenant or role where your compliance team can download reports and artifacts. 2) API-driven pulls — we provide audit log endpoints and signed S3 exports for longer-term storage. For private deployments we can also push evidence into your S3 in your account.
[00:01:48] Lena: Does Trust Center allow granular RBAC? We need separation of duties — compliance people should not be able to change config.
[00:01:55] Maya: Yes. RBAC in the console supports role types. We also support SSO enforcement so users are provisioned via SAML and SCIM to map groups to roles.
[00:02:05] Priya: About SAML — any IdP constraints? We use Okta and Azure AD.
[00:02:09] Diego: Both supported. We can give you SAML metadata and the ACS endpoints. SCIM v2 for user/group provisioning is supported; provisioning sync runs every 5 minutes by default but that's configurable.
[00:02:21] Ethan: Important: we need SCIM to not auto-provision admin roles without approval. Is there a safe default?
[00:02:27] Diego: Default role mapping sets provisioned users to a base user role; admins must be explicitly assigned to admin groups. We'll show the mappings in the demo.

[00:02:40] Tom: On contract side, what's the typical turnaround for security review? We have internal procurement SLA of 2 weeks once we get the SOC2/ISO docs.
[00:02:48] Maya: We'll prioritize sending the artifacts today/tomorrow. If NDA is needed we'll sign quickly.

[00:02:55] Priya: For audit logs — what fields do you capture? We need user, action, resource, IP, timestamp, and request/response IDs for chainability. Also retention options.
[00:03:06] Diego: Our logs include actor (user id), action verb, resource path, client IP, timestamp, request id, and often a small request metadata blob. For model inferences we also log model id, prompt hash (optional), token count, and latency. Retention: hosted plans default to 90 days, with add-on retention up to 7 years. For Dedicated/Private you can keep logs in your own account indefinitely.
[00:03:28] Priya: Prompt hash — is that reversible? We need to ensure PII isn't being stored.
[00:03:33] Diego: We store an irreversible hash by default. If you need prompt redaction we can enable a pipeline to strip PII before logs are persisted. We'll need to discuss latency tradeoffs for that.

[00:03:50] Ethan: Data residency — Sentinel needs EU only for certain workflows. Can we pin model serving to eu-central-1 and restrict transits?
[00:03:57] Maya: Yes, you can route requests to a specific region. For Hosted we have regional clusters; Dedicated allows reserving GPUs in a region. For Private on-prem we serve entirely in your network.
[00:04:09] Ethan: For VPC peering / private connectivity, do you support PrivateLink or direct peering?
[00:04:14] Diego: We support AWS PrivateLink and VPC peering for Dedicated. For Hosted there's an edge-to-edge secure tunnel option. We'll share examples of topology.

[00:04:28] Lena: Encryption. Is BYOK supported? We require KMS control for keys for some PHI flows.
[00:04:33] Diego: BYOK is supported for Dedicated and Private. You can bring your KMS key (AWS KMS or GCP CMEK) and we support HSM-backed keys for additional controls. For hosted customers we offer managed keys but we do have a customer-managed key option on enterprise plans.
[00:04:50] Priya: In the BYOK model, can Redwood access plaintext or are keys only used in service-side encryption?
[00:04:56] Diego: Keys are used for encryption at rest. In BYOK we still perform in-memory decryption to serve inference, so plaintext is in process memory on the inference node. For stricter models we offer a private deployment where keys never leave your environment and the inference runs on your private infra. We'll capture that as a follow-up.

[00:05:20] Priya: Regarding control mapping — we have a matrix with our control IDs. We need Redwood to map Redwood controls to our IDs and indicate evidence type and location.
[00:05:29] Maya: We can prefill the mapping. Diego, we usually provide a control mapping template that maps our control IDs to COSC / NIST / ISO controls and then you can add your company's control IDs.
[00:05:39] Diego: Yes, we'll send the template. It contains columns: our control id, control description, evidence type (report, log, config snapshot), evidence location (Trust Center link or S3 path), and frequency.

[00:05:52] Ethan: For evidence delivery, we'd prefer automated S3 exports into our account on a push schedule. Is that available?
[00:05:58] Diego: For Dedicated/Private yes. For Hosted we can set up signed S3 exports. There's also an API endpoint to pull zipped evidence bundles on request.

[00:06:10] Tom: Any red flags on the license or contract side from security reviews?
[00:06:14] Maya: Generally customers ask for SOC2 attachments, indemnity clauses, and data processing addendum (DPA). We have standard language for healthcare customers. Procurement, we'll coordinate on the DPA attachments.

[00:06:28] Priya: A technical nit: can you provide schema for logs? We want JSON schema for ingestion into our SIEM.
[00:06:34] Diego: We will provide the schema. It includes top-level fields like timestamp, actor.id, actor.type, action, resource.type, resource.id, request.id, ip_address, and meta fields. We'll send example payloads.

[00:06:48] Maya: Quick note: some of the nomenclature in the docs may show 'read wood' or 'read-wood' in transcript if auto captions did weird stuff, but the docs we'll send are clean PDFs.
[00:06:57] [laughter]

[00:07:05] Priya: About ISO scope: we need to confirm which systems are in scope. Are model weights and inference runtime included?
[00:07:12] Diego: Our ISO scope includes the inference service and control plane. We will send the scope statement — essentially model storage, serving, CI/CD, and control plane are included; weights are covered under our secure storage controls.

[00:07:26] Lena: We also need to know the control owner for incident response and who to contact for evidence requests during audits.
[00:07:31] Maya: We'll provide a contact list — primary security POC, SOC owner, and compliance mailbox. Diego will include names and escalation steps in the trust pack.

[00:07:44] Ethan: Can we get an SLA-backed retention for logs? We need guaranteed retention for 2 years for some data.
[00:07:50] Diego: For Dedicated we can contract a retention SLA. Hosted we can offer add-ons; confirm details in the contract.

[00:08:02] Priya: A scenario: if we need to demonstrate an incident timeline for an audit, how quickly can Redwood produce correlated logs for a 30-day window?
[00:08:11] Diego: For Hosted, on-demand evidence bundles can be prepared within 48 hours for standard requests. For Dedicated/Private, since logs are in your account, you can query immediately. We'll include SLAs in the follow-up.

[00:08:26] Maya: I want to call out one thing — model outputs. If you have PHI or regulated inputs, we recommend either Private deployment or strict isolation on Dedicated with BYOK and retained logs in your account. We can walk through the tradeoffs in the SE deep-dive.

[00:08:40] Priya: Understood. That tradeoff is core.

[00:08:43] Diego: Also, regarding network egress — if you need no egress to public internet, Private on-prem is the right pattern. For cloud Dedicated, we can lock routing to region and peer VPCs.

[00:08:55] Ethan: Any differences in evidence format between Hosted and Dedicated? We want consistent JSON logs for ingestion.
[00:09:01] Diego: We maintain a consistent schema across modes; only difference is the delivery method.

[00:09:07] Priya: Can we get an auditor-friendly report that lists mapping to our controls and shows evidence links?
[00:09:12] Maya: Yes — that's a standard deliverable. We'll generate a mapping sheet with linkable evidence and a control narrative.

[00:09:20] Tom: Procurement question — are there any one-time setup fees for Trust Center access or SSO setup?
[00:09:25] Maya: Usually no for SSO; there may be professional services fees for bespoke integrations or private deployments. We'll surface that in the quote.

[00:09:33] Lena: A compliance detail: how long do you retain metadata about deleted users? We have a policy to keep certain artifacts for 1 year.
[00:09:40] Diego: Deleted user metadata is retained per your retention policy; default is 90 days but can be extended. For Dedicated we can match your 1-year retention requirement contractually.

[00:09:52] Priya: Can Redwood redact outputs when customers request? For example, in post-processing pipelines?
[00:09:58] Diego: We have post-processing hooks and can integrate redaction pipelines. That will be part of the implementation work.

[00:10:07] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps — we'll send the SOC2 and ISO artifacts, the control mapping template prefilled, SAML metadata and SCIM notes, and a proposed time for the SE deep-dive. Anything else?
[00:10:18] Priya: Please include the log schema and sample payloads.
[00:10:21] Ethan: And the VPC peering example topology.
[00:10:24] Lena: Confirm retention options in writing.
[00:10:26] Tom: And pricing addendum for retention and BYOK.

[00:10:30] Maya: Perfect. We'll follow up with those artifacts by next week. Thanks everyone.
[00:10:35] Priya: Thank you.
[00:10:37] Ethan: Thanks.
[00:10:39] Lena: Thanks all.
[00:10:41] [meeting ends - small chitchat fades out]
